items.title: Holiday checkstop season starts in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Drivers are being reminded not to get behind the wheel after consuming alcohol or drugs as holiday checkstops return to Mississauga and Brampton. The Peel Regional Police Festive Reduce Impaired Driving Everywhere (RIDE) campaign kicked off on Friday. The annual road safety campaign will see officers conduct roadside checks throughout Brampton and Mississauga. Festive RIDE is aimed at reducing alcohol and drug-impaired driving “while promoting responsible choices behind the wheel during one of the busiest travel periods of the year,” police say. Since 2024, Peel police say officers have investigated more than 35,000 vehicles, conducted nearly 13,000 screening tests and laid 186 impaired driving charges under the RIDE program. The campaign runs during the holiday season through to New Year’s Eve. A total of 123 people were charged during the six-week campaign last year. Peel police say they inspected 16,101 vehicles at spot checks and conducted 6,443 roadside screening tests. In 2024, 126 impaired driving charges and 373 charges overall (749 fewer than 2025 Holiday RIDE) were laid by Peel police during their 2024 Holiday Season RIDE campaign. “Impaired driving remains one of the leading causes of criminal death in Canada and continues to pose a significant risk to public safety,” Peel police say.

items.title: No refunds for cancelled Mississauga comedy festival as organizers declare bankruptcy
items.summary: Ticket holders for a cancelled comedy festival in Mississauga may never get their money back after the company behind the event filed for bankruptcy, leaving customers who have been waiting months for refunds facing an uncertain financial future. , the company behind the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival, made an assignment in bankruptcy effective November 13, with MNP Ltd. appointed as the Licensed Insolvency Trustee. The development is particularly bad news for people who purchased tickets to the festival’s planned Mississauga debut at Erindale Park, which was postponed just three days before it was scheduled to begin in September. Tickets were not cheap, with general admission prices ranging from $39 to $99 depending on the performance. General admission plus tickets ranged from $49 to $129, while VIP table seating started at $69 for some shows and reached $169 for others. VIP Club tickets were advertised for as much as $499, before applicable fees. At the time of the postponement, organizers said they were exploring new dates and promised to follow up directly with ticket holders. But no replacement dates were announced, and customers from across Ontario complained they were unable to get answers about refunds despite repeated attempts to contact the company. As previously reported by Insauga, ticket buyers were left wondering what happened to the Mississauga festival after organizers abruptly pulled the plug. A subsequent report detailed how the massive event was postponed just days before opening, leaving customers and the local community with unanswered questions. Now, with Trixstar bankrupt, outstanding ticket claims must be directed to the company’s bankruptcy trustee rather than the festival organizer.

items.title: Councillor Sets Up Meetings as CAPREIT Pitches 150-Plus New Townhouses at Two Mississauga Sites
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca has scheduled back-to-back community meetings so residents can question developer CAPREIT about two proposed townhouse additions. The outlet reported the plans would add more than 150 townhouses to existing apartment properties at 1055 Bloor Street and 2121 Rathburn Road East. One session will focus on 1055 Bloor Street, where CAPREIT wants to add 112 stacked townhouse units to the existing building, insauga.com said. That proposal already hit a snag in August, when it went before the city's Committee of Adjustment seeking 19 variances. Fonseca said planning staff and committee members raised concerns about parking and traffic impacts, according to the outlet. The committee's staff report recommended deferring the application until the developer worked further with the councillor's office and nearby residents, the outlet reported.

items.title: Francique's Parents Describe Devastating Loss on Opening Day of Peel Police Inquest
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Jamal Francique's parents delivered tearful statements on the first day of the coroner's inquest into his death nearly seven years after Peel police shot him. The outlet reported Derek Francique and Ann-Marie White described their son as a smart, considerate son and devoted father whose loss shattered their family. Derek Francique said his son was always the glue that held their family together and that they are destroyed without him, according to insauga.com. He said the family hopes the inquest brings a fuller understanding of police tactics and whether anti-Black racism played a role in officers' decisions. White said she is not simply grieving a past event but living with the loss and pain every day, the outlet reported. The inquest, which began Friday, is examining the circumstances of Francique's fatal shooting during a 2020 arrest attempt.

items.title: Three Decades of Volunteer Work Built Ontario's School Cricket Program to 5,000 Students
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga volunteer Ranil Mendis has spent more than three decades expanding school access to cricket for newcomer families whose kids once had few chances to play it. The outlet reported Mendis built partnerships with school boards and community groups to bring the sport into gym classes. His work helped grow a school cricket program that now reaches more than 5,000 Ontario students a year, according to the Ontario Schools Cricket Association, where Mendis serves as a board member, insauga.com said. The program traces to a CIMA Canada initiative aimed at introducing cricket to students from diverse backgrounds, the outlet reported. Mendis helped overcome barriers that had long kept the sport out of many schools, according to the report. His work recently earned him the 2026 Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year, insauga.com noted.

items.title: Major Roads and Bus Routes Come First as Mississauga Readies Winter Snow Crews
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga crews are on standby around the clock to clear roads and sidewalks once snow begins falling across the city this season. The outlet reported the municipality follows a priority system that determines which streets get cleared first and how long residents may wait for their own street. Major roads, priority sidewalks, bus stops, crossings and bike lanes are cleared first to keep routes safe for emergency vehicles, transit and drivers, insauga.com said. Lots and entrances at community centres, arenas and libraries are also part of that first wave, according to the outlet. Crews then move on to residential roads and secondary sidewalks. The city said priority routes typically take 12 to 24 hours to clear, while residential streets take 24 to 36 hours, though back to back storms or heavy snowfall can extend those timelines, insauga.com reported.

items.title: Metrolinx Weighs Demolishing 1903 Credit River Rail Bridge in Port Credit
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Metrolinx is preparing to demolish the Credit River Railway Bridge in Port Credit, just west of the Port Credit GO Station. The outlet reported the plan surfaced in a letter from Giaimo and Associates Architects to the Town of Port Credit Association, which said the firm was retained to prepare a Heritage Impact Assessment on the structure. Insauga.com said the bridge, built in 1903 and twinned in 2008, carries two railway tracks east to west across the Credit River between Stavebank Road and Mississauga Road. Structural inspections found the bridge in poor condition and determined it could not be rehabilitated, the letter said. The bridge carries GO Transit, Via Rail and freight operations, and any replacement must keep meeting Transport Canada rules while allowing for future GO service growth, insauga.com reported.

items.title: Hospitality Worker Collects $7-Million Lump Sum After Winning Daily Grand's Top Prize
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Mississauga hospitality worker James Lui-Yee won the Daily Grand's top prize of $1,000 a day for life, but chose the $7 million lump sum payout instead. The outlet reported the winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada on Burnhamthorpe Road West. Lui-Yee said he did not check the ticket until two weeks after the draw and initially thought the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation app had made an error. He said his heart raced once he manually confirmed his numbers matched the winning combination at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto. Lui-Yee said he plans to seek financial advice before making major decisions, but hopes to buy a home, invest and travel to Greece, Portugal and Spain, Mississauga.com reported. He also looks forward to buying a new phone and an advanced chessboard, according to the outlet.

items.title: Use-of-Force Training and Anti-Black Racism Among Issues as Francique Inquest Opens
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has begun after being delayed a day from its original Thursday start. The outlet reported Francique, a 28-year-old Black man, was shot by Peel Regional Police during an attempted arrest outside his home on Jan. 7, 2020, and died in hospital days later. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit later cleared the officers, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, the Star said. The SIU noted there were still questions about the officer's conduct, including his decision to position himself near a fleeing vehicle, according to the report. The inquest will examine police procedures on use of force involving vehicles, oversight of planned arrests, medical care for incapacitated suspects and anti-Black racism, the Toronto Star reported.
